items.label: HB_ITEM_ANT
items.fact_en: A queen of this little black garden ant can live for up to 29 years.

items.label: HB_ITEM_LADYBIRD
items.fact_en: The seven-spot ladybird has three spots on each wing case and one shared in the middle.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BEE
items.fact_en: A busy hive can hold as many as 60,000 worker bees.

items.label: HB_ITEM_LEGO_BRICK
items.fact_en: A standard 2x4 Lego brick is only about 3 cm long, yet millions of combinations come from such bricks.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SNAIL
items.fact_en: A Roman snail can live for 20 years, and its shell grows along with it.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GOLF_BALL
items.fact_en: A golf ball has about 300 to 500 dimples on its surface.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TENNIS_BALL
items.fact_en: Tennis balls turned yellow in 1972 so they would show up better on television.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CRICKET_BALL
items.fact_en: A cricket ball has a cork core wound with string and covered in leather.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FROG
items.fact_en: The edible frog is a cross between two other frogs, the pool frog and the marsh frog.

items.label: HB_ITEM_RUBY_THROATED_HUMMINGBIRD
items.fact_en: A ruby-throated hummingbird can beat its wings about 50 times a second.

items.label: HB_ITEM_MOUSE
items.fact_en: A house mouse's tail can be as long as the rest of its body.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BUTTERFLY
items.fact_en: Monarchs fly up to 2,800 miles to spend the winter in Mexico's mountain forests.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BEVERAGE_CAN
items.fact_en: A standard 355 ml drink can is only about 12 cm tall, yet holds a full cup and a half of liquid.

items.label: HB_ITEM_EUROPEAN_ROBIN
items.fact_en: Robins sing through winter, and both males and females defend territories.

items.label: HB_ITEM_HOUSE_SPARROW
items.fact_en: House sparrows have lived alongside people for thousands of years, often picking crumbs near shops.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PENCIL
items.fact_en: A standard pencil's hexagonal shell is only about 7 millimetres across.

items.label: HB_ITEM_VOLLEYBALL
items.fact_en: A volleyball has a standard circumference of about 65 to 67 centimetres, a size fixed by the rules.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BOWLING_BALL
items.fact_en: A bowling ball can weigh up to 7 kg yet fits a standard diameter of about 21.6 cm.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FOOTBALL
items.fact_en: The laws of the game ask for a ball 68 to 70 cm around, which makes it this wide.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CRAB
items.fact_en: Its scientific name means 'savoury beautiful swimmer'.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CAT
items.fact_en: Cats sleep 12 to 16 hours a day.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BASKETBALL
items.fact_en: An official basketball is about 75 cm around its middle.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GUINEA_PIG
items.fact_en: Guinea pigs are not pigs and not from Guinea; they come from the Andes and are rodents.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BLACKBIRD
items.fact_en: Male blackbirds are glossy black with orange-yellow beaks, and they often feed on lawns near breakfast tables.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ATLANTIC_PUFFIN
items.fact_en: Atlantic puffins carry several small fish crosswise in their bill to feed chicks.

items.label: HB_ITEM_MOORHEN
items.fact_en: Moorhens bob their white undertail when they swim and flick it as a warning.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ROCK_PIGEON
items.fact_en: Rock pigeons were tamed thousands of years ago and now live in almost every city in the world.

items.label: HB_ITEM_RABBIT
items.fact_en: A rabbit's ears are 7 to 8 cm long, about a fifth of its whole body.

items.label: HB_ITEM_EURASIAN_COOT
items.fact_en: Coots have lobed toe flaps, not webbed feet, to paddle through water.

items.label: HB_ITEM_EURASIAN_OYSTERCATCHER
items.fact_en: Oystercatchers use their long bills to pry open mussels and cockles on the shore.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CHICKEN
items.fact_en: There are more than 26 billion chickens, over three for every person on Earth.

items.label: HB_ITEM_RING_BILLED_GULL
items.fact_en: Gulls can drink seawater because a gland near the eyes filters out the excess salt.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DOG
items.fact_en: A Labrador stands 55 to 57 cm at the shoulder, a good middle among big dogs.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BEER_KEG
items.fact_en: A standard US half-barrel keg holds about 58 litres of beer.

items.label: HB_ITEM_MALLARD_DUCK
items.fact_en: Mallard ducklings can swim within hours of hatching.

items.label: HB_ITEM_HERRING_GULL
items.fact_en: Herring gulls can live over 30 years in the wild.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FIRE_EXTINGUISHER
items.fact_en: The first portable fire extinguishers were soda-acid models, filled with water and a bottle of acid.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SHEEP
items.fact_en: A sheep's slit-shaped pupils let it see behind itself without turning its head.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TRAFFIC_CONE
items.fact_en: Traffic cones are orange so drivers can spot them from far away.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FIRE_HYDRANT
items.fact_en: Fire hydrants are painted in different colours in different countries so firefighters can tell their water supply apart.

items.label: HB_ITEM_EUROPEAN_BADGER
items.fact_en: Badger setts can be used by the same family of badgers for generations.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GREYLAG_GOOSE
items.fact_en: Greylag geese often form pair bonds that last for many years, and families stay together through the winter.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SKATEBOARD
items.fact_en: A standard street skateboard deck is about as long as a adult's forearm and hand.

items.label: HB_ITEM_COMMON_PHEASANT
items.fact_en: The male pheasant's long tail can make up more than half of its total length.

items.label: HB_ITEM_WASHING_MACHINE
items.fact_en: Early washing machines were hand-cranked tubs before electric drums became the standard design.

items.label: HB_ITEM_OIL_DRUM
items.fact_en: The standard 200-litre steel drum has been used for shipping liquids for more than a century.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CANADA_GOOSE
items.fact_en: Canada geese often return to the same lake or pond where they were born.

items.label: HB_ITEM_KING_PENGUIN
items.fact_en: King penguins can dive deeper than 300 metres in search of fish.

items.label: HB_ITEM_HONEY_BADGER
items.fact_en: Honey badgers are famous for fearlessly taking on animals much larger than themselves.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ROCKING_CHAIR
items.fact_en: The rocking chair was patented in the United States in 1867 and is still made to a similar pattern.

items.label: HB_ITEM_RED_FOX
items.fact_en: Red foxes can hear prey squeaking under snow and pounce through the snow to catch it.

items.label: HB_ITEM_WILD_TURKEY
items.fact_en: Wild turkeys can fly short distances and roost high in trees at night.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PENGUIN
items.fact_en: Emperor penguins dive deeper than 500 metres and stay under for 20 minutes.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CAPYBARA
items.fact_en: The capybara is the largest rodent in the world and often shares water with other animals.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GOAT
items.fact_en: Goats have rectangular pupils that give them a wide view of their surroundings.

items.label: HB_ITEM_UPRIGHT_PIANO
items.fact_en: An upright piano's strings run vertically inside the case, which is why it can stand against a wall.

items.label: HB_ITEM_EURO_PALLET
items.fact_en: Euro pallets share one standard size, so warehouses across Europe can use any of them.

items.label: HB_ITEM_COW
items.fact_en: A Holstein gives about 10,000 kg of milk a year, some 27 litres every day.

items.label: HB_ITEM_HORSE
items.fact_en: Horses are measured at the withers, and they can sleep standing up.

items.label: HB_ITEM_MUTE_SWAN
items.fact_en: Despite its name, the mute swan makes hissing, grunting and snorting sounds.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PIG
items.fact_en: Pigs have few sweat glands, so they roll in mud to keep cool.

items.label: HB_ITEM_WHEELBARROW
items.fact_en: A wheelbarrow puts most of its load over one wheel, which makes it easy to push.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PERSON
items.fact_en: Around the world, men average about 171 cm tall and women about 160 cm.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BATHTUB
items.fact_en: Early bathtubs were often made of copper or cast iron before acrylic became the common material.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BICYCLE
items.fact_en: A road bike is longer than its rider is tall.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PARK_BENCH
items.fact_en: The word bench comes from a long seat built against a wall.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DOUBLE_BASS
items.fact_en: The double bass is the largest and lowest-pitched bowed string instrument in the orchestra.

items.label: HB_ITEM_REINDEER
items.fact_en: Both female and male reindeer grow antlers.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DOOR
items.fact_en: Most house doors are 80 inches tall, so nearly everyone walks under without ducking.

items.label: HB_ITEM_OSTRICH
items.fact_en: One ostrich egg holds about as much as two dozen chicken eggs.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DONKEY
items.fact_en: Donkeys were domesticated from African wild asses about 5,000 years ago.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TAPIR_BRAZIL
items.fact_en: A tapir's flexible snout works like a short trunk for grabbing leaves.

items.label: HB_ITEM_POLAR_BEAR
items.fact_en: Polar bears have black skin under their white fur.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TELEPHONE_BOX
items.fact_en: The classic red K6 kiosk, designed by Giles Gilbert Scott, stands about 2.4 m tall.

items.label: HB_ITEM_LION
items.fact_en: A lion's roar can be heard from about 8 kilometres away.

items.label: HB_ITEM_POOL_TABLE
items.fact_en: A standard 9-foot pool table has a playing surface of 2.54 m by 1.27 m.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SMART_FORTWO
items.fact_en: The Smart fortwo is so short it fits two of them in one regular parking space.

items.label: HB_ITEM_MOOSE
items.fact_en: Only male moose grow antlers, and they can span over 1.5 m.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TABLE_TENNIS_TABLE
items.fact_en: A table tennis table is exactly 2.74 metres long, the same size in every official match.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GRAND_PIANO
items.fact_en: A concert grand piano has roughly 12,000 separate parts.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PLAINS_ZEBRA
items.fact_en: Each plains zebra has a unique stripe pattern, like a fingerprint.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DROMEDARY_CAMEL
items.fact_en: A dromedary can drink about 100 litres of water in ten minutes after days without drinking.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CLASSIC_MINI
items.fact_en: The original Mini was so compact that its designers fitted the engine sideways to save space.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ELEPHANT
items.fact_en: The African bush elephant is the largest animal walking on land.

items.label: HB_ITEM_HIPPO
items.fact_en: A hippo can hold its breath underwater for up to about five minutes.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FIAT_500
items.fact_en: The original Fiat 500 was small enough to fit inside a modern car's boot... roughly.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SNOOKER_TABLE
items.fact_en: A full-size snooker table has a playing area twice as long as it is wide.

items.label: HB_ITEM_INDIAN_RHINOCEROS
items.fact_en: The Indian rhinoceros has a single horn and armour-like folds of skin.

items.label: HB_ITEM_VW_BEETLE
items.fact_en: The Volkswagen Beetle was built for over 60 years, and its classic shape stayed almost the same.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CROCODILE
items.fact_en: The saltwater crocodile is the largest reptile alive today.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CAR
items.fact_en: A family hatchback is about as long as two and a half people lying head to toe.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SHARK
items.fact_en: A great white has about 300 serrated teeth and keeps growing new ones.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GIRAFFE
items.fact_en: A giraffe's long neck has just seven bones, the same number as yours.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SHIPPING_CONTAINER_20FT
items.fact_en: Every standard 20-foot shipping container is built to the same size, so ships and trucks can carry any of them.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ORCA
items.fact_en: A male orca's back fin stands 1.8 metres tall, higher than most people.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ROUTEMASTER_BUS
items.fact_en: London's Routemaster double-decker ran on city streets for about 50 years.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BUS
items.fact_en: A city bus is almost exactly as long as a T. rex.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SCHOOL_BUS
items.fact_en: School buses are painted yellow so drivers can spot them more easily on busy roads.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TREX
items.fact_en: Sue, one of the most complete T. rex skeletons, is more than 12 metres long.

items.label: HB_ITEM_WHALE
items.fact_en: The blue whale is the largest animal ever known; its heart alone weighs 180 kg.
